prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my configuration is unchanged: one prize part, B041, to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The case rests on the science, not on the six matching opening ranks. GLP-1 is a complete arc from the incretin effect and the physiology of the gut hormone, through identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form and its actions on islets, gut and appetite circuits, to a drug class with large independent randomised outcome evidence in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. It defined a hormone axis, it has been confirmed over decades and its impact is at its peak, so the timing is right. On the chair's first question, I would anchor the citation in physiology and the active peptide. That is the discovery, and it is the only framing that fits a three-name limit without turning the prize into a ranking of drug products. A single-achievement prize is preferable here: a second part would force B041 down to two names and would make the Knudsen gap harder, not easier, to explain.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point and nothing in round 1 resolved it. Knudsen's long-acting analogue design is what put the drugs in patients' hands, and a physiology citation leaves it out. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested, and Habener and other contributors outside the credited list may have claims. I cannot verify the historical priority record from the files I am allowed to read, and I notice that no member has named which of the three would yield to Knudsen. That silence is informative: without a documented ground to displace anyone, I will not displace anyone. If the committee decides that the drug-design step is the essential achievement, my configuration is the wrong three. I also accept the point made by several colleagues that near-unanimity may partly reflect the salience of the weight-loss drugs, so I have tested the case against B030 on maturity and credit clarity. B030 is equally mature, but I still judge B041 ahead on originality and breadth.

responses.point: Sandberg places Knudsen's long-acting analogue chemistry on the product side of the line, and says that waiting on B041 would cost little if the credit question cannot be resolved because CAR-T is equally mature.
responses.response: I still agree on the allocation but not on describing Knudsen's work as merely product development. The drugs patients receive are her designs, and the committee should say openly that the physiology trio leaves a real gap. On waiting, I disagree. The credit uncertainty in B041 is about one contested priority claim and one excluded name, whereas CAR-T carries its own open question about Eshhar and the chimeric receptor originators and about Rosenberg. Neither prize is cleaner, so the credit question does not by itself justify deferring the stronger discovery. I keep B030 as my first alternative for the reason you give, equal maturity, not as a place to park the decision.

responses.point: Perlmann proposes B030 to June and Sadelain only and would reopen B041 only if the citation were framed around the drugs, warning that a prize weighted to translational success could look like a prize for commercial impact.
responses.response: I take the commercial-impact warning seriously, and it is the reason I want the B041 citation worded on physiology and the active peptide. On B030 I moved toward your narrowing in round 1 and I stay there: the CAR-specific discovery is June's and Sadelain's, and Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer work is a broader lineage. I would make the same point about Eshhar, whom I cannot assess from the supplied material. A two-name B030 is therefore the most defensible second part if the committee wants one, but I would not build the prize around it, because that cuts B041 to two names.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, keeps B035 as an alternative for its mechanistic clarity and clean two-person attribution, and asks which criterion should decide the strongest alternative to B041.
responses.response: I share the weight you give to a clean two-person allocation, and Walter and Mori are the neatest credit among the basic-mechanism candidates. On your question, I would decide the strongest alternative first on demonstrated effect on the biology and practice of medicine, and second on credit clarity. By that order B030 and B039 come ahead of B035, because the translational thread for the unfolded protein response, the integrated stress response, is still developing and the PERK arm and Ron's work sit outside the credited names, as El-Manira also notes. I would not let mechanistic elegance outrank a discovery that has already changed clinical care.

responses.point: El-Manira keeps optogenetics as an alternative but doubts that a research tool fits a discovery prize, and notes that six credited names compete for three places.
responses.response: I agree the method is transformative and well confirmed. I weigh the tool objection differently: the prize has honoured methods when they opened new biology, and optogenetics clearly has. The real obstacle is crowded credit, and I note that your trio and mine are the same, Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann, which leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck. Because the clinical effect is still early, I keep B039 only as an alternative. If the committee returned to it, I would want the citation to name the channelrhodopsin discovery and its application together, and I would accept that any trio carries a visible omission.

responses.point: Linnarsson would not dismiss Rosenberg's adoptive transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials as clinical proof of concept for B030.
responses.response: That is a fair point and I do not dismiss Rosenberg's early trials. My difficulty is the question the chair posed: what is the specific CAR-related discovery being honoured. His work is foundational for cell therapy generally, and I rank it as a lineage the citation can acknowledge in prose. It is not, in my reading, a reason to give him one of three places in a CAR-specific part. If the committee prefers a three-name B030, I would not call it indefensible, but I would prefer the narrower two-name configuration.

uncertainties: Whether Knudsen's drug-design contribution should displace one of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov. No documented ground in the supplied record identifies which of the three would give way.
Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and the roles of Habener and others outside the credited list, which I cannot verify from the files I may read.
For B030, how to treat the originators of the chimeric receptor concept such as Eshhar, and whether Rosenberg belongs in a CAR-specific part.
Whether a single-achievement prize is better than a two-part prize, given that any second part forces B041 to two names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile for B041, B030 or B039. My field is rheumatology and autoimmunity, so B026 (TNF blockade) and B031 (cGAS-STING) are close to my expertise; neither is in my preferred configuration or my alternatives. I will recuse if a documented co-author or close institutional tie to any credited name emerges. No new disclosure arose from reading the round-1 statements.
